title: Dative 6: Motion Toward (к + dative)
description: The preposition к (toward) takes the dative case. Used with motion verbs: 'Я иду к маме' (I'm going to mom).
descriptionRussian: Предлог 'к' (по направлению к) требует дательного падежа. Используется с глаголами движения.
intro: One preposition takes this case, and it means going toward. The distinction worth getting right is between going to a person and going into a place: Russian uses this preposition for the first and a different one for the second. Going to your mother and going to school are built differently, and mixing them up is the commonest mistake here.
rules: К is the one common preposition that takes the dative case. It expresses MOTION TOWARD a person or thing: к маме, к брату, к окну.
К pairs with motion verbs: идти, ехать, подходить, приходить, etc. The dative form of the target follows the same rules as Lesson 1.
Use к for motion toward PEOPLE; use в + accusative for motion INTO a building. 'Я иду к маме' (to mom) vs 'Я иду в школу' (to school).
examples: Я иду к маме. (I'm going to mom.) мама → маме (dat fem -а).
Антон едет к брату. (Anton is going (by transport) to brother.) брат → брату (dat masc).
Маша подходит к окну. (Masha is approaching the window.) окно → окну (dat neuter -о).
Лена идёт к Антону. (Lena is going to Anton.) Антон → Антону (dat masc).
Я иду к тёте. (I'm going to aunt.) тётя → тёте (dat fem -я).
Антон подходит к морю. (Anton is approaching the sea.) море → морю (dat neuter -е).

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 5: which form of я is the state experiencer?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 5: the state experiencer is dative. Я → мне. Today's lesson keeps the dative but adds a new trigger: the preposition к.

items.hint: К takes which case? Apply the feminine rule from Lesson 1.
items.explanation: К is the one preposition that takes the dative. Мама is feminine -а: -а → -е → маме. The whole phrase 'к маме' means 'to mom' (toward mom).

items.promptEnglish: Anton is going to his brother.
items.hint: Брат is masculine consonant. Apply the dative rule.
items.explanation: Брат → брату. Ехать paired with к expresses 'going (by transport) to a person.' The form is the same dative -у you've used since Lesson 1.

items.hint: Окно is neuter -о. Apply the neuter dative rule.
items.explanation: Окно → окну. К + dative also works for motion toward inanimate things. Подходить к + dat is the standard 'approach' construction.

items.hint: Тётя is feminine -я. The dative ending is...?
items.explanation: Тётя → тёте. Soft -я swaps to -е, parallel to fem -а → -е.

items.hint: Антон is masculine consonant. Same masculine rule.
items.explanation: Антон → Антону. Names follow the same dative rules as common nouns. Ехать к + dat means 'going (by transport) to (a person).'

blanks: Антон подходит к _____. (Anton is approaching the sea.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Море is neuter -е. К + dative neuter -е takes -ю → морю. К works with both animate (people) and inanimate (sea, window) targets of motion.

minimalPairs.explanation: К takes the dative. Мама → маме. The nominative мама does not appear after a preposition; only the dative form is grammatical here.

К takes the dative. Брат → брату. The same word would appear in different forms after different prepositions: 'у брата' (gen, at brother's place), 'о брате' (prep, about brother), 'к брату' (dat, toward brother).

errorCorrection.explanation: К governs the dative, so мама → маме: к маме. The nominative мама cannot follow a preposition. The dative answers 'к кому?' (toward whom).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton is going to his brother.
errorCorrection.explanation: К takes the dative: брат → брату (masculine consonant + -у). К брат leaves the bare nominative, which never follows a preposition. After к, the target of motion is dative: к брату.

Motion toward a PERSON uses к + dative, not в: к маме. В marks motion into or location inside a place (в школу, в школе), so в маме would mean 'inside mom', which makes no sense. The contrast is к (toward a person or thing) versus в (into or inside a building).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The cat quietly approaches the window.
errorCorrection.explanation: К governs the dative, and neuter nouns ending in -о swap -о for -у: окно → окну, so к окну. Подходить к + dative is the standard 'approach' construction, and к works for things as well as people: к окну.

errorCorrection.sentence: В воскресенье я иду к тётю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: On Sunday I am going to my aunt's.
errorCorrection.explanation: К takes the dative, and feminine nouns in -я swap -я for -е: тётя → тёте, so к тёте. Тётю is the accusative, which к does not govern. The soft -я becomes a soft -е, parallel to feminine -а → -е.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша часто ходит к сестра в гости.
errorCorrection.explanation: К governs the dative, and feminine -а nouns swap -а for -е: сестра → сестре, so к сестре. The phrase 'ходить к кому в гости' means 'to visit someone'. Сестра is the bare nominative, which never follows a preposition.

reviewVocab.definition: toward (preposition + dative; pairs with motion verbs to express direction toward a person or thing)
to go (on foot / by transport, one direction); both pair with к + dative
reviewVocab.example: Я иду к брату. Антон едет к другу.

reviewVocab.definition: to approach (always paired with к + dative: подходить к + dat)
